title: Motorcycle Manufacturing Concessionary Regime
summary: The policy evolved from a simple CKD-based incentive scheme for motorcycle assembly in 2016 to a more structured, category-based manufacturing framework. Over time, the regulatory focus shifted from initial assembly incentives to rigorous monitoring of input-output coefficients (UD) and the formalization of manufacturer categories (Category-1 and Category-2) to distinguish between deep manufacturing and assembly.

evolution.legal_basis: Transitioned from Customs Act 1969/VAT Act 1991 to VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012 and Customs Act 2023.
evolution.classification: Evolved from a general assembly incentive to a tiered system (Category-1 and Category-2) based on local value addition and manufacturing depth.
evolution.monitoring: Standardized the use of 'Input-Output Coefficients' (Parishishta-2) and mandatory 6-month physical inspections.

timeline.change: Initial introduction of duty concessions for CKD motorcycle assembly and local production incentives.
Introduction of formal definitions for 'Motorcycle Manufacturing Institution' and 'Vendor', and requirement for input-output coefficient (UD) submission.
Formalization of 'Category-1' and 'Category-2' manufacturing classifications and transition to the VAT and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012 framework.
Amendment to the definition of Category-1 manufacturing institutions under the Customs Act, 2023.

Customs Act 1969: Section 19(1) of this Act provides the legal authority for the government to grant duty and tax exemptions to encourage local industrial production.
Imported Vehicle: This order applies to motorcycles with engine capacities greater than fifty cubic centimeters but less than two hundred fifty cubic centimeters that feature a four-stroke engine.
The exemption framework specifically covers motorcycles imported in completely knocked-down condition to support the transition to local assembly and manufacturing.
Industrial Unit: Manufacturers engaged in the local assembly or production of the specified motorcycles are eligible for duty and tax waivers on imported components, parts, and raw materials used in the production process.
National Board of Revenue: The government issues this order and grants the associated duty exemptions in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
H.S. Code: The order provides a detailed schedule of components and parts categorized by their respective Heading and H.S. Code that qualify for tax and duty concessions when imported for motorcycle manufacturing.

CKD Motorcycle Import and Local Producti: Qualified importers and manufacturers may receive an exemption on Supplementary Duty exceeding a specific percentage for the import of motorcycles in completely knocked-down (CKD) condition, subject to approval from the Ministry of Industries.
The exemption is valid for a period of two years from the date of approval, provided that the customs clearance and assessment process for the imported goods are completed within this timeframe.

After the expiration of the two-year exemption period, importers are no longer eligible for concessional rates under the CKD scheme and must instead transition to local progressive manufacturing of motorcycle components to continue receiving benefits.

Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty A: This notification is issued under the authority of section 126(1) of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act 2012.
National Board of Revenue: The Government issued this notification after consultation with the National Board of Revenue.
Local Production of Motorcycle Parts: This order provides duty concessions on the import of specific inputs and parts for the purpose of promoting the local production of motorcycles with designated engine capacities.
The order specifies different duty reduction tiers for different categories of local motorcycle manufacturers and vendors.
TABLE-I: This table lists specific H.S. codes for chemical, plastic, and metal components eligible for duty concessions under the local motorcycle production scheme.
TABLE-II: This table identifies mechanical and electrical components, including engine parts and chassis components, subject to specific duty concessions when imported for local motorcycle manufacturing.
TABLE-III: This table lists specific chassis and structural motorcycle parts eligible for duty concessions when imported by category-2 manufacturers.

Industrial IRC Holder: To qualify for import concessions, an industrial entity must hold an updated and renewed industrial IRC.
Entities operating under the control of specific government authorities that do not require an industrial IRC must instead submit an import permit issued by their respective regulatory authority.
VAT Compliant: An importer must be a 13-digit Value Added Tax compliant entity that has filed their required VAT returns for the month immediately preceding the filing of the Bill of Entry.
Compliance status must be verifiable through the customs computer system, VAT online system, or the official website of the National Board of Revenue or the relevant VAT Commissionerate.
In cases of force majeure or logical inability to access electronic data, the Commissioner of Customs may authorize clearance by recording the reasons for the exception.
Motorcycle Manufacturing Industrial Esta: This category is divided into Category-1 and Category-2 based on the complexity of locally produced or imported parts and assembly processes.
Entities that only import motorcycles in completely knocked down (CKD) condition with a pre-made chassis and other parts are excluded from these concessions.

Category-1 manufacturers must produce all parts or the chassis and specific important parts locally. Category-2 manufacturers produce the chassis and important parts from smaller imported or locally sourced components.
Vendor: A Vendor is defined as a VAT-registered manufacturing entity that produces motorcycle parts using locally sourced or imported raw materials.
Vendors must supply these parts to motorcycle manufacturing establishments under specific sales agreements or local supply arrangements.
Industrial Import Concession: Eligible Category-1 manufacturers and vendors may import goods listed in TABLE-I and TABLE-II under concessional rates.
Category-2 manufacturers are permitted to import goods listed in TABLE-II and TABLE-III under these concessions.
Value Added Tax: Category-1 manufacturers qualifying for Category-2 benefits must submit a verified input-output coefficient declaration (VAT-4.3) for each motorcycle model, certified by the relevant VAT departmental officer, at the time of customs clearance.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue maintains the electronic systems through which VAT compliance and industrial registration status must be verifiable for importers.
